summary.headline: Orient Electric Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR948 crores and EBITDA margin improved to 8.2%, though gross margin fell to 31% on commodity inflation.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR948 crores, up 10% YoY, with Lighting and Switchgear up 16% and ECD up 7.6%. EBITDA rose 15.8% to INR77 crores (8.2% margin) and PAT rose 28.9% to INR40 crores, despite gross margin compressing to 31% from commodity inflation, labour shortage and West Asia gas disruption. For FY26, revenue grew 7.5% to INR3,326 crores, EBITDA rose 12.4% to INR229 crores (about 6.9% margin), and PBT before exceptional items rose 24.2% to about INR139 crores. Calibrated price increases of about 4% in Q4 and roughly 6% in April were taken, and management said these do not fully offset cost inflation.

financial_highlights.change: Hit by commodity inflation; about 100-150 bps impact from March price-action lag

segments.name: Lighting and Switchgear
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY on distribution expansion and premiumisation; consumer lighting grew double digits. High-value luminaires rose to 68% of mix from 63%; professional luminaires were flat. Wires roughly doubled, and switches and switchgear grew high double digits.

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7.6% YoY despite industry softness. Fans grew high single digit; BLDC grew over 50% and is 25% of domestic ceiling fan revenue. Premium mix is about 35% of domestic fan revenue, up from 30% last quarter.

segments.name: Appliances and e-commerce
segments.commentary: Appliances (heating, garment care) grew high double digits and e-commerce grew high double digits; quick commerce is 10% of digital channel. Exports grew double digits, with TPW a significant part.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 demand to improve, supported by a forecast of a hotter, more prolonged summer and a possible late-season surge in fans and cooling.
Further calibrated price increases are possible if commodity inflation continues; the company says cost recovery is a priority but competitiveness must be preserved.
Management remains committed to reaching double-digit EBITDA margins structurally once commodity inflation and supply disruptions subside; no specific timeline was given.
Gross margin guidance of 32-34% is unchanged, with Q4 running about 100-150 bps below it.
No FY27 numerical guidance was given; no share buyback is planned at present.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant utilisation is improving; TPW production is split between Kolkata and Hyderabad, and the plant is a hub for southern and export supply.
Hyderabad capex has been completed, per an analyst question; management did not add detail.
New products include Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching fan, about INR16,000), Aerosilent (under 50 dB, about INR8,000) and an inverter battery backup fan (about 6 hours of backup).
demand_pricing: Price increases: about 2.5-3% in January, 1-1.5% in March, and about 6% in April; fans, lighting and switchgear each about 6%, and wires increased roughly every 2-3 weeks.
Management says the incremental cost impact was slightly lower than the industry because part of its portfolio needed little spec change.
Market share gained about 30-40 bps per third-party data, described as broad-based across channels and markets, not limited to BLDC.
Channel inventory was elevated, and dealers were cautious on replenishment; Q4 channel build was described as normal.
Consumer offtake is about 45% in March-June and 55% in the balance of the year; premium and BLDC demand is more linear.
Cost pressure: labour shortage, commercial LPG unavailability, and minimum wage hikes of 35% in Haryana and 24% in UP.

qa_highlights.question: How much more price hike is needed to pass on the full incremental cost, and where are the fan market share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the price action was staggered (about 4% in Q4, about 6% in April) and the incremental impact was lower than the industry. Market share gains of 30-40 bps were broad-based across channels, not confined to BLDC.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise to over 30 from 23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher inventory built to hedge supply disruptions and higher payables.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the double-digit EBITDA margin target slipped, and when will it be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 100-150 bps gross margin hit from the lag in price action in March. It remains committed to double-digit margins once commodity inflation and supply disruptions ease, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has gross margin not improved despite a higher premium mix and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases do not fully offset commodity inflation, and labour productivity, LPG costs and wage hikes add further cost pressure. Premiumisation has helped EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2026 a year of protecting margins, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY26 was a washout and H2 exited with better EBITDA margins. It gave no numerical FY27 guidance and said challenges remain.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing now a structural tailwind toward INR3,000 crore revenue and INR100 crore profit over FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see this as pricing power, calling it a catch-22 industry situation. It pointed to consumer-led product value as the real pricing power and said the aim is INR5,000 crore revenue with double-digit EBITDA.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation, the West Asia conflict, and gas and LPG supply disruption could keep gross margin below the 32-34% guidance band.
Elevated channel inventory and cautious dealer replenishment could weigh on Q1 FY27 primary sales.
Demand depends on a hot, prolonged summer; Q1 weather has been mixed.
Working capital days rose to over 30 from 23 on inventory build and payables; watch the unwind.
Price increases may face elasticity limits; management says competitiveness is being preserved.
Hyderabad plant utilisation and cost absorption; the plant is still a fixed-cost drag.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and premiumisation, but cautious and defensive on margins and the FY27 outlook. Management attributed the margin miss to commodity and supply shocks and declined to give FY27 numbers or a timeline for double-digit EBITDA.
key_quotes: So it's never going to be either a DTM or MD, it's going to be a balance of both, provided either of the model delivers what the expectation on these few parameters that I spoke about.
I don't see it as a pricing power. I think it's a catch-22 situation that the industry has got into and I'm largely reflecting from an industry perspective right now.
Given the commodity inflation to subside and supply disruptions to go away, from a structural perspective, we are trending towards a double-digit margin.

growth.why: No numerical FY27 guidance; gross margin 32-34% and double-digit EBITDA margin are held but without timelines, and the Hyderabad capex is completed with no new capacity detail, so growth backing is vague (pricing, share gains and a hotter summer forecast).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin rose to 8.2% (about +40 bps YoY) and FY26 margin was about 6.9%, but gross margin fell to 31% against 32-34% guidance with 100-150 bps lag from March price action; double-digit margin has no timeline and depends on commodity inflation easing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hyderabad capex is already completed with no new capacity detail given, and no new plant, line or store additions were announced; the call points to utilisation improving at Hyderabad rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects Q1 FY27 demand to improve on a hotter, more prolonged summer, and market share gained 30-40 bps; Q4 revenue grew 10% YoY and Lighting and Switchgear grew 16%, though channel inventory is elevated and dealers are cautious on replenishment.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond the completed Hyderabad build, and no utilisation figure was given, so there is no basis for a new capex call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given, and management described challenges remaining with gross margin running 100-150 bps below the 32-34% band in Q4.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin ran about 31% in Q4 against a 32-34% guide; commodity inflation, LPG unavailability, and wage hikes of 35% in Haryana and 24% in UP could keep it below band, and Q1 primary sales face channel inventory and a weather-dependent summer.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aero O2 (about INR16,000), Aerosilent (under 50 dB, about INR8,000) and an inverter battery backup fan (about 6 hours of backup) are named as new products, and BLDC is 25% of domestic ceiling fan revenue, growing over 50%.

rows.label: Further calibrated price increases
rows.why: Price rises of about 4% in Q4 and about 6% in April did not fully offset cost inflation, and management said further hikes are possible if commodity inflation continues.

rows.label: Working capital days unwind
rows.why: Working capital days rose to over 30 from 23 on inventory built to hedge supply disruptions and higher payables, and the unwind is a watch item.

rows.label: Export and southern supply from Hyderabad
rows.why: Exports grew double digits with TPW a significant part, and the Hyderabad plant is a hub for southern and export supply with utilisation improving.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, premiumisation and share gains (30-40 bps), but cautious and defensive on margins, declining FY27 numbers or a timeline for double-digit EBITDA; analysts pushed on the margin miss, gross margin recovery and whether pricing is a structural tailwind.
